findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Split AC2 into an in-session check (verify the container receives the three env vars from a seeded-or-fixture SSM value and bridge_check_access no longer exits 2) versus a post-operator-seed activation check, and mark the live-credential verification as explicitly deferred to operator seeding.
evidence: AC: 'bridge_check_access returns its typed verdict rather than exit 2.'
OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED: 'The credential VALUES must be seeded into SSM by a human... The code can land inert and activate when the parameters are populated.'
This is a post-operator-action verification, not evaluable via repo artifacts / closing PR CI within one session.
findings.finding: AC2 ('bridge_check_access returns its typed verdict rather than exit 2') cannot be evaluated in-session because it requires live Jira credentials that OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED states are seeded by a human and may not exist at merge time; the plan itself says the code 'can land inert and activate when the parameters are populated'.
scenarios: PR merges with correct wiring but no seeded SSM values; AC2 remains unverifiable and the reviewer cannot confirm done-ness.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe AC2 as: 'With test/placeholder SSM values present, bridge_check_access reaches Jira config resolution (no longer exit 2 for missing config); live-token verification is deferred to operator seeding and recorded on the ticket.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct Work step 3: the three JIRA vars are SSM->.env values, so DON'T spell them as `-e` in mcp_run_new and DON'T list them in the compose `environment:` block; they reach both containers via the existing `env_file: .env` / `--env-file`. If they are listed in compose (for documentation) add them to `_ENV_FILE_ONLY` in test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py, mirroring MCP_TICKETS_PAT.
evidence: Work: 'Pass them to the mcp container in BOTH infra/compose/docker-compose.yml AND autodeploy.sh's mcp_run_new … the compose-parity test pins this'
docker-compose.yml mcp service uses `env_file: - .env` (line 331); mcp_run_new uses `--env-file "$COMPOSE_DIR/.env"` (autodeploy.sh:371) — .env vars flow with no per-key listing

test:867 `_ENV_FILE_ONLY = frozenset({"MCP_TICKETS_PAT"})` and test:898-901 assert `-e {key}=` must NOT be present for env-file-only keys; MCP_TICKETS_PAT is the SSM->.env single-line precedent the JIRA vars mirror
docker-compose.yml:388 spells the precedent as `MCP_TICKETS_PAT: "${MCP_TICKETS_PAT:-}"` and it is env-file-only
findings.finding: Work step 3 ('Pass them to the mcp container in BOTH docker-compose.yml AND mcp_run_new') is the wrong mechanism for SSM->.env values and will BREAK the compose-parity test the plan itself relies on. The mcp compose service and mcp_run_new both already load the entire .env (env_file: .env / --env-file), so a fetch-secrets-written var reaches the container automatically without any `environment:`/`-e` entry. Spelling JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN as `-e VAR=${VAR:-}` in mcp_run_new resolves to EMPTY (docker run does not interpolate) and clobbers the real .env value — precisely the hazard `_ENV_FILE_ONLY` (currently just MCP_TICKETS_PAT) exists to prevent; test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service asserts env-file-only keys must NOT appear as `-e`. Conversely, listing them in compose `environment:` without adding them to `_ENV_FILE_ONLY` makes the same test demand a matching `-e` and fail.
scenarios: Implementer follows step 3 literally, adds `-e JIRA_API_TOKEN=${JIRA_API_TOKEN:-}` to mcp_run_new -> blank clobbers the .env token -> bridge_check_access still fails; parity test also fails
Implementer adds the three keys to compose `environment:` -> parity test demands matching `-e` in mcp_run_new -> CI red
findings.suggested_fix: Follow the MCP_TICKETS_PAT precedent exactly: rely on --env-file/env_file to carry all three vars; if you document them in compose environment: as `${JIRA_*:-}`, extend `_ENV_FILE_ONLY` to include them so the parity oracle stays green.

_lib_ops.py:366-368 raises RebarError(message, returncode=2, stderr=message) whenever run_access_check returns 2 — there is no soft 'not configured' branch
Work steps 1-4 name only ssm.tf / fetch-secrets.sh / docker-compose.yml / autodeploy.sh — no edit to _lib_ops.py or access_check.py
findings.finding: AC3 ('Absent credentials degrade softly with a clear "not configured" report') is not delivered by any Work step. bridge_check_access() raises RebarError(returncode=2) on missing creds (_lib_ops.py:362-368) and access_check has no 'not configured' soft verdict; the Work section changes only infra wiring (ssm.tf, fetch-secrets.sh, docker-compose.yml, autodeploy.sh), never the bridge code path. With the parameters landing as CHANGEME/blank first (per OPERATOR ACTION), the ABSENT-creds case is the DEFAULT post-deploy state, yet the tool will still raise exit 2 rather than emit a 'not configured' report.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 3 vs Work section; src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:362-368
scenarios: Code lands inert (operator hasn't seeded SSM) -> a client calls bridge_check_access -> it still raises exit 2, not a 'not configured' report -> AC3 fails on the very state the plan expects at first deploy

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make Work step 2 explicit that all three JIRA leaves are read via get_param_optional (never get_param), so a CHANGEME/blank slot leaves a blank .env value and boots the stack, per the soft-degrade posture in step 4.
evidence: fetch-secrets.sh:58-60 get_param aborts on empty/None/CHANGEME; get_param_optional (69-81) yields blank instead
OPERATOR ACTION: 'The code can land inert and activate when the parameters are populated' — i.e. CHANGEME/blank at first deploy
Work step 4: 'Absent Jira credentials should degrade softly … must NOT take the endpoint down'
findings.finding: Work step 2 ('Emit them from fetch-secrets.sh') does not specify get_param vs get_param_optional, but the soft-degrade posture (step 4) and the inert-until-seeded model force get_param_optional. fetch-secrets.sh's get_param ABORTS the whole run (exit 1, no .env written) on an empty/None/CHANGEME value; since the JIRA params land as CHANGEME first, using get_param would fail every boot and take ALL containers down — directly violating AC3's 'the endpoint stays up'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify Step 3 so the JIRA vars are carried env-file-ONLY (the MCP_TICKETS_PAT precedent + `_ENV_FILE_ONLY`), not re-spelled as `-e`/`environment:` in mcp_run_new/compose, to avoid config-surface duplication and the `${KEY:-}`-clobbers-.env trap.
evidence: Plan: 'Pass them to the mcp container in BOTH infra/compose/docker-compose.yml AND autodeploy.sh's mcp_run_new'
docker-compose.yml:331 mcp service already `env_file: - .env`; autodeploy.sh:371 `--env-file "$COMPOSE_DIR/.env"`

The exact env-file-only precedent MCP_TICKETS_PAT is in test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:867 `_ENV_FILE_ONLY = frozenset({"MCP_TICKETS_PAT"})`, whose comment: 're-spelling them as `-e` would overwrite the real value with an empty string'
docker-compose.yml:388 spells MCP_TICKETS_PAT as `${MCP_TICKETS_PAT:-}` — i.e. env-file-carried, not a mandatory `-e`
findings.finding: Step 3 proposes passing JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN to the mcp container in BOTH docker-compose.yml AND mcp_run_new, but both already carry the container .env (compose `env_file: - .env`; `mcp_run_new --env-file "$COMPOSE_DIR/.env"`), so once Step 2 writes the vars into .env they reach both containers with no per-var container edit; adding explicit `-e`/`environment:` lines is redundant config surface and, for a `${KEY:-}`-spelled value, actively wrong.
scenarios: An implementer reads 'pass to BOTH' literally and adds `-e JIRA_URL=${JIRA_URL:-}` to mcp_run_new plus a mirrored `environment:` block, duplicating surface that env_file already covers and (for the `${KEY:-}` form) clobbering the .env value with an empty string.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the new jira-url / jira-user / jira-api-token parameters follow the existing ssm.tf convention (placeholder value + `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`) so operator-seeded values are not reverted on the next apply.
evidence: ssm.tf:80-89 creates every secret slot with `value = "CHANGEME"` and `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }` so 'terraform owns the parameter's existence + type, not its value'
Plan Work step 1 only says: 'Declare the parameters ... as String / SecureString' with no ignore_changes / placeholder note
Plan's OPERATOR ACTION section relies on operator-seeded values that must survive re-apply
findings.finding: The plan declares new SSM parameters but does not adopt the existing ssm.tf drift-avoidance convention (CHANGEME placeholder value + lifecycle{ignore_changes=[value]}), so a later `terraform apply` could revert the operator-seeded Jira values back to the placeholder.
scenarios: Operator seeds /rebar/prod/jira-api-token, a later apply runs, and Terraform overwrites it back to a placeholder — silently re-breaking the bridge.
findings.suggested_fix: In Work step 1, state that the three parameters are declared with a CHANGEME placeholder value and `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [value] }`, matching the existing `rebar_secrets` resource, so Terraform owns existence+type only, not the operator-set value.

If step 3 adds them to the compose environment: block as `${JIRA_URL:-}` without adding them to _ENV_FILE_ONLY, the parity test fails demanding `-e JIRA_URL=` in mcp_run_new.
Plan quote: 'the compose-parity test pins this' and AC '...asserted to agree by the existing parity test' — the plan names the oracle but not the frozenset edit it forces.

findings.checklist_item: State that fetch-secrets.sh reads the three Jira leaves via get_param_optional (not the fail-fast get_param) so unpopulated/CHANGEME values yield blanks and the container boots, matching the chosen soft-degrade posture.
evidence: fetch-secrets.sh:48-63 get_param aborts with exit 1 on empty/None/CHANGEME (fail-fast)
fetch-secrets.sh:69-81 get_param_optional yields empty and never aborts — the documented mechanism for soft-degrading creds
Plan Work step 4: 'Absent Jira credentials should degrade softly ... and must NOT take the endpoint down' but Work step 2 only says 'Emit them from fetch-secrets.sh'
findings.finding: The plan mandates a soft-degrade failure posture but does not specify that fetch-secrets.sh must read the Jira leaves via get_param_optional; the default get_param reader is fail-fast and aborts on empty/CHANGEME, which would contradict the stated soft-degrade goal.
scenarios: Author wires the Jira leaves through get_param (the required reader); with the parameters seeded as CHANGEME placeholders, fetch-secrets.sh aborts at boot and takes cloud-init/the endpoint down — the opposite of the stated soft-degrade posture.
findings.suggested_fix: In Work step 2, specify the get_param_optional path for jira-url / jira-user / jira-api-token (as done for the OPTIONAL OAuth / tickets-PAT leaves) so a blank slot defers bridge availability rather than aborting the boot.

findings.checklist_item: Confirm and record how the existing SecureString-only `for_each` in ssm.tf and the `--with-decryption`/`CHANGEME` fetch flow will accommodate `String`-typed jira-url/jira-user params (e.g. a separate resource or per-leaf type map), since no in-repo `String` SSM precedent exists.
evidence: Plan: "Declare the parameters ... /rebar/prod/jira-url and /rebar/prod/jira-user as `String`, /rebar/prod/jira-api-token as `SecureString`."

infra/terraform/ssm.tf:80-85 — a single `aws_ssm_parameter "rebar_secrets"` with `for_each = toset(local.rebar_secret_params)` and `type = "SecureString"` for ALL leaves; search for `type = "String"` in infra/terraform returned (no matches).
infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:48-63 — get_param/get_param_optional read every leaf with `--with-decryption` and abort/blank on the `CHANGEME` sentinel, machinery shaped for SecureString slots.
findings.finding: The plan asserts a URL/USER-vs-TOKEN split by declaring jira-url/jira-user as SSM `String` and jira-api-token as `SecureString`, but there is no in-repo precedent for a `String`-typed SSM parameter: infra/terraform/ssm.tf creates EVERY /rebar/prod/* param through one `for_each` over `rebar_secret_params` hard-coded to `type = "SecureString"`, and fetch-secrets.sh reads all leaves with `--with-decryption` plus a `CHANGEME` fail-fast sentinel. The plan does not verify that the existing single-type for_each and decryption-based fetch machinery accommodate a plaintext String slot.
findings.location: Work step 1 ("/rebar/prod/jira-url and /rebar/prod/jira-user as String") and the "URL/USER-vs-TOKEN split" rationale
scenarios: The new String params can't be added to the existing SecureString-only for_each without a second resource block or a per-leaf type map — an implementer following the plan literally hits a structural mismatch.
fetch-secrets.sh's SecureString-oriented read/sentinel flow is applied to a plaintext String value that terraform seeds without CHANGEME semantics.
